claim:
Let \(R_\lambda^2=(\mathbb R^2,N_\lambda)\), where \(1<\lambda\le\sqrt2\) and
\[
N_\lambda(u,v)=\max\{\lambda|u|,\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\}.
\]
For \(\varepsilon\in[0,1)\), write \(a\perp_D^\varepsilon b\) when
\[
N_\lambda(a+t b)\ge\sqrt{1-\varepsilon^2}\,N_\lambda(a)
\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).
\]
Then the least \(\varepsilon\) such that
\[
x\perp_B y\Longrightarrow y\perp_D^\varepsilon x
\qquad(x,y\in R_\lambda^2)
\]
is
\[
\varepsilon_D(R_\lambda^2)=\sqrt{1-\lambda^{-2}}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\inf_{\substack{x,y\in S_{R_\lambda^2}\\x\perp_B y}}
\inf_{t\in\mathbb R}N_\lambda(y+t x)=\frac1\lambda.
\]
Equality is attained at
\[
x=\left(\frac1\lambda,\sqrt{1-\lambda^{-2}}\right),
\qquad y=(0,-1),
\]
and at their images under the sign symmetries.
integrity: The proof exhausts all unit-sphere strata and computes reverse line distance exactly from annihilating dual functionals. The corner endpoint gives the sharp value; no numerical optimization is used.
scientific_limitations: The exact formula is proved only for the first Banaś--Frączek regime 1<lambda<=sqrt(2). The second regime has different corner geometry and is not covered. A differently notated exact treatment outside the checked sources remains a bibliographic risk.
title: Sharp Dragomir symmetry parameter on the first Banaś--Frączek regime
